questions.explanation: Formal announcements use 'declared', and 'you' becomes 'he' based on context.

questions.prompt: Convert to indirect speech: He said, 'I had finished before she came.'
options: He said that he had finished before she came.
He said that he had had finished before she had come.
He said that he had finished before she had come.
He told that he had finished before she had come.
questions.explanation: Past perfect 'had finished' does not change; 'came' can optionally become 'had come'.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a correct reporting verb for requests?
questions.explanation: 'Requested' is the most appropriate verb for polite requests.

questions.prompt: Convert to indirect speech: She said, 'I need your help.'
options: She said that she needed my help.
She said that she needs your help.
She said that she needed his help.
She told that she needed my help.
questions.explanation: 'Need' (present) becomes 'needed' (past), and 'your' becomes 'my' based on context.

questions.prompt: What does 'ago' change to in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: 'Ago' becomes 'before' in reported speech (e.g., 'two days ago' becomes 'two days before').

questions.prompt: Convert to indirect speech: 'Wait here,' he said to me.
options: He told me to wait there.
He told me to wait here.
He said me to wait there.
He asked me to wait here.
questions.explanation: 'Told' is used with an object, and 'here' becomes 'there'.

questions.prompt: What is the correct punctuation for direct speech?
questions.explanation: A comma is placed after the reporting verb and before the opening quotation mark.

questions.prompt: Convert to indirect speech: He said, 'I have been waiting since morning.'
options: He said that he had been waiting since morning.
He said that he has been waiting since morning.
He said that he had been waiting from morning.
He told that he had been waiting since morning.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous becomes past perfect continuous; 'since' does not change.

questions.prompt: Convert to indirect speech: She said, 'How wonderful!'
options: She exclaimed that it was wonderful.
She told that it was wonderful.
questions.explanation: Exclamations with 'how' use 'exclaimed that it was...' structure.

questions.prompt: What does 'this evening' change to in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: 'This evening' becomes 'that evening' in reported speech.

questions.prompt: Convert to indirect speech: He said, 'I could have done better.'
options: He said that he could have done better.
He said that he had been able to do better.
He said that he can have done better.
He told that he could have done better.
questions.explanation: 'Could' does not change in reported speech.

questions.prompt: What reporting verb is used for saying goodbye?
questions.explanation: 'Bade' is used for saying goodbye (e.g., 'He bade me farewell').

questions.prompt: Convert to indirect speech: She said, 'I must go now.'
options: She said that she had to go then.
She said that she must go now.
She said that she had to go now.
She told that she had to go then.
questions.explanation: 'Must' (obligation) usually becomes 'had to', and 'now' becomes 'then'.

questions.prompt: Convert to indirect speech: 'Why did you do that?' he asked.
options: He asked why I had done that.
He asked why did I do that.
He asked why I did that.
He asked me why had I done that.
questions.explanation: Past 'did do' becomes past perfect 'had done' in reported speech.

questions.prompt: What is the first word inside quotation marks?
questions.explanation: The first word inside quotation marks always begins with a capital letter.

questions.prompt: Convert to indirect speech: He said, 'I am busy now.'
options: He said that he was busy then.
He said that he is busy now.
He said that he was busy now.
He told that he was busy then.
questions.explanation: 'Am' becomes 'was', and 'now' becomes 'then'.

questions.prompt: What reporting verb is used for denying something?
questions.explanation: 'Denied' is used when someone says something is not true.

questions.prompt: Convert to indirect speech: She said, 'I haven't seen him for ages.'
options: She said that she hadn't seen him for ages.
She said that she hasn't seen him for ages.
She said that she hadn't seen him since ages.
She told that she hadn't seen him for ages.
questions.explanation: Present perfect negative 'haven't seen' becomes past perfect negative 'hadn't seen'.

questions.prompt: What does 'tonight' change to in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: 'Tonight' becomes 'that night' in reported speech.

questions.prompt: Convert to indirect speech: He said, 'Let's have dinner.'
options: He suggested that they should have dinner.
He said that let's have dinner.
questions.explanation: 'Let's' suggestions use 'suggested that...should' structure.

questions.prompt: What does 'last year' change to in indirect speech?
questions.explanation: 'Last year' becomes 'the year before' or 'the previous year' in reported speech.

questions.prompt: Convert to indirect speech: She said, 'I might come later.'
options: She said that she might come later.
She said that she may come later.
She said that she could come later.
She told that she might come later.
questions.explanation: 'Might' does not change in reported speech.

questions.prompt: Which of these sentences uses correct indirect speech?
options: He said that he would come the next day.
He said that 'he would come tomorrow.'
He said that he will come tomorrow.
He told that he would come next day.
questions.explanation: Correct indirect speech uses 'would', no quotation marks, and 'the next day' instead of 'tomorrow'.

questions.prompt: Convert to indirect speech: The doctor said, 'Take this medicine twice a day.'
options: The doctor advised him to take that medicine twice a day.
The doctor told him to take this medicine twice a day.
The doctor said him to take that medicine twice a day.
The doctor ordered to take that medicine twice a day.
questions.explanation: Medical instructions use 'advised', 'this' becomes 'that', and the object is required.

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between direct and indirect speech?
options: Quotation marks are used in direct but not in indirect
Word order is always the same
questions.explanation: The main visible difference is the use of quotation marks in direct speech only.

questions.prompt: Convert to indirect speech: He said, 'I was tired so I went to bed early.'
options: He said that he had been tired so he had gone to bed early.
He said that he was tired so he went to bed early.
He said that he had been tired so he went to bed early.
He told that he had been tired so he had gone to bed early.
questions.explanation: Both 'was' and 'went' backshift to 'had been' and 'had gone' respectively.

questions.prompt: Convert to indirect speech: She said, 'I am sorry I broke your vase.'
options: She apologized for breaking my vase.
She said that she was sorry she had broken my vase.
She regretted that she broke my vase.
All of the above are correct
questions.explanation: All three options are acceptable ways to report this apology in indirect speech.

questions.prompt: Which end mark correctly completes this sentence: 'Where is the nearest hospital___'
questions.explanation: A direct question asking for information requires a question mark.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: She asked where he was going?
She asked where he was going.
She asked, where he was going?
She asked where he was going!
questions.explanation: Indirect questions embedded in statements end with a period, not a question mark.

questions.prompt: Where should commas be placed: 'However we must leave now.'
questions.explanation: 'However' is an introductory transitional word that requires a comma after it.

questions.prompt: Add commas: 'I bought apples oranges and bananas.'
options: I bought apples, oranges, and bananas.
I bought, apples, oranges and bananas.
I bought apples oranges, and bananas.
I bought apples oranges and, bananas.
questions.explanation: Commas separate items in a series. The Oxford comma before 'and' is recommended for clarity.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses commas correctly with a compound sentence?
options: I wanted to go but I stayed home.
I wanted to go, but I stayed home.
I wanted to go but, I stayed home.
I wanted, to go but I stayed home.
questions.explanation: A comma before the coordinating conjunction 'but' is required when joining two independent clauses.

questions.prompt: Correct the comma usage: 'My brother who is a doctor lives in Paris.'
options: My brother, who is a doctor, lives in Paris.
My brother who is a doctor, lives in Paris.
My brother, who is a doctor lives in Paris.
My brother who is a doctor lives, in Paris.
questions.explanation: Nonessential clauses (who is a doctor) need commas both before and after.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a semicolon?
options: I love reading; and I read daily.
I love reading; it is my favorite hobby.
I love reading; but I have no time.
I love reading,; it is my hobby.
questions.explanation: A semicolon correctly joins two closely related independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct punctuation: 'She studied hard___ therefore___ she passed.'
questions.explanation: Use a semicolon before and a comma after transitional words like 'therefore.'

questions.prompt: Punctuate this list correctly: 'We visited Paris France Rome Italy and Madrid Spain.'
options: We visited Paris, France; Rome, Italy; and Madrid, Spain.
We visited Paris France, Rome Italy, and Madrid Spain.
We visited Paris, France, Rome, Italy, and Madrid, Spain.
We visited Paris; France; Rome; Italy; and Madrid; Spain.
questions.explanation: When list items contain commas, use semicolons to separate the main items.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct colon usage: 'Bring the following___ pencils paper and erasers.'
options: Bring the following: pencils, paper, and erasers.
Bring the following; pencils, paper, and erasers.
Bring the following, pencils, paper, and erasers.
Bring the following- pencils, paper, and erasers.
questions.explanation: A colon correctly introduces a list that follows a complete sentence.

questions.prompt: Which shows correct singular possessive form?
questions.explanation: For singular nouns, add 's to show possession: dog's.

questions.prompt: Which shows correct plural possessive form?
questions.explanation: 'Children' is plural but doesn't end in s, so add 's: children's.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly?
questions.explanation: This is plural (more than one Smith), not possessive. No apostrophe needed.

questions.prompt: Punctuate correctly: 'She said I am leaving now.'
questions.explanation: Use a comma after the dialogue tag and place the period inside the quotation marks.

questions.prompt: Where does the question mark go: Did she say, 'I am leaving'___
questions.explanation: The question mark goes outside the quotation marks because the entire sentence is a question, not the quoted words.

questions.prompt: Format correctly: 'Wait' he shouted 'do not go'
questions.explanation: Use commas inside quotation marks when dialogue is interrupted by a tag, and lowercase the continuation if it's the same sentence.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct punctuation for a number range: 'Read pages 15___25.'
questions.explanation: Use an en dash (–) for number ranges, not a hyphen (-).

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses an em dash?
options: The students - all ten of them - passed.
The students - all ten of them — passed.
questions.explanation: Em dashes (—) set off parenthetical interruptions without spaces around them.

questions.prompt: Which punctuation correctly completes: 'What a beautiful day___'
questions.explanation: An exclamation point shows strong emotion or emphasis.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: I wanted to go, but I could not.
I wanted to go but I could not.
I wanted, to go but I could not.
I wanted to go but, I could not.
questions.explanation: A comma + coordinating conjunction is needed to join two independent clauses.

questions.prompt: Where should commas go: 'In the morning the birds sing loudly.'
options: In the morning, the birds sing loudly.
In, the morning the birds sing loudly.
In the morning the birds, sing loudly.
In the morning the birds sing, loudly.
questions.explanation: An introductory prepositional phrase requires a comma after it.

questions.prompt: Punctuate correctly: 'John please close the door.'
questions.explanation: Use a comma to set off a name when directly addressing someone.

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses an apostrophe in a contraction?
questions.explanation: The apostrophe replaces the omitted letter 'o' in 'do not': don't.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct possessive: 'The ___ room is clean.' (belonging to James)
questions.explanation: Singular nouns ending in s still take 's for possessive: James's.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly punctuated dialogue: 'I am hungry' said John 'let us eat.'
options: 'I am hungry,' said John, 'let us eat.'
'I am hungry' said John, 'let us eat.'
'I am hungry,' said John 'let us eat.'
'I am hungry said John let us eat.'
questions.explanation: When interrupting dialogue, use commas inside the quotation marks around the tag.

questions.prompt: Which end mark is correct: 'The train arrives at 9 PM___'
questions.explanation: This is a declarative statement, so it ends with a period.

questions.prompt: Correct the punctuation: 'She asked, where are you going.'
options: She asked, where are you going?
questions.explanation: Direct questions inside quotation marks need the question mark inside the quotes.

questions.prompt: Where do commas belong: 'Because it was raining we stayed inside.'
options: Because, it was raining we stayed inside.
Because it was raining, we stayed inside.
Because it was raining we, stayed inside.
Because it was raining we stayed, inside.
questions.explanation: An introductory dependent clause needs a comma after it before the main clause.

questions.prompt: Which correctly punctuates a series: 'I like reading writing and drawing.'
options: I like reading, writing and drawing.
I like reading, writing, and drawing.
I like, reading, writing, and drawing.
I like reading writing, and drawing.
questions.explanation: Commas separate items in a series, with the Oxford comma recommended before 'and.'

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: She wanted to leave; but she stayed.
She wanted to leave but she stayed.
She wanted to leave, but she stayed.
She wanted to leave; but, she stayed.
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction need a comma before the conjunction.

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses a semicolon with a transitional word?
options: I was tired; however I continued.
I was tired, however, I continued.
I was tired; however, I continued.
I was tired: however; I continued.
questions.explanation: Use a semicolon before and a comma after transitional words like 'however.'

questions.prompt: Choose the correct colon usage: 'Remember this___ always be kind.'
questions.explanation: A colon introduces a statement or rule that follows a complete sentence.

questions.prompt: Which shows correct joint possession?
questions.explanation: For joint ownership, add 's only to the last noun: John and Mary's house (they share one house).

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses an apostrophe with 'it'?
questions.explanation: 'It's' is the contraction for 'it is.' 'Its' (no apostrophe) is the possessive pronoun.

questions.prompt: Format correctly: 'I do not know' she replied 'what you mean.'
options: 'I do not know,' she replied, 'what you mean.'
'I do not know' she replied, 'what you mean.'
'I do not know,' she replied 'what you mean.'
'I do not know she replied what you mean.'
questions.explanation: When interrupting dialogue, commas go inside the quotation marks before and after the tag.

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses quotation marks with other punctuation?
questions.explanation: When the entire sentence is a question but the quote is not, the question mark goes outside.

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses parentheses?
options: The concert (which was long) was good.
The concert which was long was good.
The concert, (which was long), was good.
The concert, which was long, was good.
questions.explanation: Parentheses enclose supplementary information. Commas are not needed with parentheses.

questions.prompt: Which end mark is correct for a command: 'Close the door___'
questions.explanation: Commands typically end with a period. An exclamation point would show strong urgency.

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses commas with dates?
questions.explanation: Use a comma between day and year, and after the year if the sentence continues.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: My brother who lives in Boston is visiting.
My brother, who lives in Boston, is visiting.
My brother who lives in Boston, is visiting.
My brother, who lives in Boston is visiting.
questions.explanation: Nonessential relative clauses need commas both before and after.

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses a semicolon?
options: I like tea; and I drink it daily.
I like tea,; it refreshes me.
I like tea; it refreshes me.
I like tea; but it is expensive.
questions.explanation: A semicolon correctly joins two related independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction.

questions.prompt: Punctuate this list: 'We need bread milk eggs and butter.'
options: We need bread, milk, eggs, and butter.
We need, bread, milk, eggs, and butter.
We need bread milk, eggs, and butter.
We need bread, milk eggs and butter.
questions.explanation: Commas separate items in a series, with the Oxford comma before the final 'and.'

questions.prompt: Choose the correct colon usage.
options: The ingredients: are flour and water.
The ingredients are: flour and water.
The ingredients are flour: and water.
The: ingredients are flour and water.
questions.explanation: A colon follows a complete sentence to introduce what comes next: a list, explanation, etc.

questions.prompt: Which shows correct plural possessive for nouns ending in s?
questions.explanation: For plural nouns ending in s, add only an apostrophe: students'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: '___ been a difficult day.' (contraction)
questions.explanation: 'It's' is the contraction for 'it has' in this context.

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses an apostrophe to show omitted letters?
questions.explanation: 'Won't' is the irregular contraction for 'will not,' with the apostrophe replacing omitted letters.

questions.prompt: Format dialogue correctly: 'Hello world' shouted the boy
questions.explanation: The exclamation point expressing excitement goes inside the quotation marks before the dialogue tag.

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses quotation marks for a quote within a quote?
options: He said, 'She told me to stop.'
He said She told me to stop.
questions.explanation: Use single quotation marks for a quote within a quote, with double quotes for the main quotation.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly hyphenated phrase.
options: a state of the art facility
questions.explanation: Compound modifiers with multiple words are hyphenated throughout: state-of-the-art.

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses an en dash?
questions.explanation: Use an en dash (–) for time ranges and number spans.

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses an ellipsis?
options: I wonder... if he will come.
I wonder.. if he will come.
I wonder....... if he will come.
I wonder. if he will come.
questions.explanation: An ellipsis consists of exactly three dots (...) to indicate a pause or trailing thought.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has correct punctuation throughout?
questions.explanation: Use a comma after the dialogue tag and place the period inside the closing quotation mark.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: I came I saw I conquered.
I came, I saw, I conquered.
I came; I saw; I conquered.
I came: I saw: I conquered.
questions.explanation: Semicolons can separate short, closely related independent clauses for dramatic effect.

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses commas with addresses?
options: She lives at 45 Oak Street New York NY 10001.
She lives at 45 Oak Street, New York, NY 10001.
She lives at 45, Oak Street, New York, NY, 10001.
She lives at 45 Oak Street New York, NY 10001.
questions.explanation: Commas separate street address from city, and city from state: 45 Oak Street, New York, NY 10001.

questions.prompt: Punctuate correctly: 'After dinner we went for a walk.'
options: After dinner, we went for a walk.
After, dinner we went for a walk.
After dinner we, went for a walk.
After dinner we went for, a walk.
questions.explanation: A short introductory prepositional phrase can take a comma for clarity, though it's optional.

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses a colon for emphasis?
options: He had one goal, to win.
He had one goal; to win.
He had one goal: to win.
He had one goal to win.
questions.explanation: A colon emphasizes what follows after a complete sentence: He had one goal: to win.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct possessive form.
questions.explanation: 'Children' is plural but doesn't end in s, so add 's: children's.

questions.prompt: Which correctly distinguishes its vs. it's?
questions.explanation: 'It's' = it is (contraction with apostrophe). 'Its' = possessive pronoun (no apostrophe).

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses brackets?
options: She said, 'I meaning myself will go.'
questions.explanation: Brackets show the speaker's own insertion/clarification within a quotation.

questions.prompt: Which end mark is correct: 'Watch out for that car___'
questions.explanation: An exclamation point expresses urgency and warning: Watch out for that car!

questions.prompt: Correct the punctuation: 'He asked if I was coming___'
options: He asked if I was coming?
He asked if I was coming.
He asked, if I was coming.
He asked if I was coming!
questions.explanation: Indirect questions embedded in statements end with a period.

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses commas with a compound predicate?
options: She ran to the door, and opened it.
She ran to the door and opened it.
She ran, to the door and opened it.
She ran to the door and, opened it.
questions.explanation: Do NOT use a comma with a compound predicate (one subject, two verbs).

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
questions.explanation: Use a comma after introductory words like 'yes,' 'no,' 'well,' etc.

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses a semicolon in a complex list?
options: We visited: Paris, France, Rome, Italy, Madrid, Spain.
We visited Paris, France; Rome, Italy; Madrid, Spain.
We visited: Paris, France; Rome, Italy; Madrid, Spain.
We visited Paris; France; Rome; Italy; Madrid; Spain.
questions.explanation: Use semicolons to separate list items that contain internal commas.

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses a colon in time notation?
questions.explanation: Use a colon to separate hours and minutes in time: 9:30.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct plural possessive.
questions.explanation: 'Men' is plural but doesn't end in s, so add 's: men's.

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses a slash?
questions.explanation: Use a slash to mean 'per' in measurements: km/hr (kilometers per hour).

questions.prompt: Which end mark is correct: 'Are you coming with us___'
questions.explanation: A direct yes/no question requires a question mark.

questions.prompt: Punctuate correctly: 'She said that she was tired___'
questions.explanation: This is a statement with an indirect quotation, so it ends with a period.

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses commas with contrasting expressions?
questions.explanation: Use a comma before 'not' when contrasting: She is smart, not lazy.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: I am studying hard; because I want to pass.
I am studying hard, because I want to pass.
I am studying hard because I want to pass.
I am studying hard: because I want to pass.
questions.explanation: 'Because' is a subordinating conjunction that introduces a dependent clause. No comma is needed when the dependent clause follows the main clause.

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses a colon after a greeting?
questions.explanation: Use a colon after formal business letter greetings: Dear Sir:

questions.prompt: Choose the correct possessive for individual ownership.
questions.explanation: For individual ownership of separate items, add 's to each noun: John's and Mary's cars (two separate cars).

questions.prompt: Which correctly uses 'there's' (contraction)?
questions.explanation: 'There's' is the contraction for 'there is,' correctly placed with the apostrophe.
